This prevents premature convergence to local minima, which is common in high-dimensional spaces. Our approach combines deterministic optimization with restarts to escape local minima at multiple scales. We justify this by the observation that non-convex optimization often benefits from directional hyperparameter sweeps guided by frequency analysis of time-constrained flips in function value distributions.

   - The core innovation is the introduction of a dimension-reduction layer (using recursive k-means) that clusters the high-dimensional space into coherent components, projecting the optimization onto meaningful feature spaces. This reduces effective dimensionality while preserving the global optimization structure.
